sources.how_to_read: Slow and rigorous; the place to test a trade belief against data.

sources.who: London; founded 1903; scholarly articles and the ‘Art market’ and ‘Exhibitions’ reviews.
sources.good_for: Attribution and provenance scholarship that moves prices; catalogue reviews; its historic ‘Art market’ column.
sources.record: No page opened this session.
sources.how_to_read: Connoisseurship; a Burlington attribution note is a market event in Old Masters.

whispers.about: Sotheby’s New York, the November calendar
whispers.t: Sotheby’s own marquee page sets The Now and Contemporary Evening Auction for 16 November at 7pm, Legendary: The Blaquier-Arrieta Collection for 18 November at 6pm and the Modern Evening Auction for 18 November at 7pm, all at 945 Madison Avenue.
whispers.detail: Exhibition 7–18 November (Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm, Sunday 1pm–5pm); the page states that a reservation is required for entry. Day auctions (Modern Day, Contemporary Day) and the Baum day and evening auctions are listed without dates on the page. No guarantee or irrevocable-bid symbols appear on the marquee page itself.

whispers.t: The house lists the Blaquier-Arrieta headline lots: Van Gogh, Châtaigniers en fleurs (lot 5) and Cézanne, Arlequin (lot 9) with estimates upon request; Pissarro, La Place du Théâtre-Français et l’avenue de l’Opéra (lot 10) US$30m–40m; Renoir, En Canot (lot 8) US$25m–35m; Degas, Avant la course (lot 7) US$20m–30m; Monet, Le Jardin des Tuileries (lot 4) US$15m–20m.
whispers.detail: The Degas, Avant la course, at US$20m–30m, did not appear in the September announcement as The Art Newspaper reported it; it is on the house’s page. The two ‘upon request’ lots are the ones the trade press carries at ‘in the region of US$180m’ (Van Gogh) and ‘around US$120m’ (Cézanne).

whispers.t: Headline lots: Magritte, L’Ami de l’ordre (lot 107) US$25m–35m; Hopper, The Martha McKeen of Wellfleet (lot 109) US$20m–30m; Cézanne, Pichet et fruits sur une table (lot 123) US$20m–30m; Signac, Collioure. Les Balancelles (Opus 167) (lot 112) US$12m–18m; Degas, Danseuse rajustant son chausson (lot 111) US$5m–7m.
whispers.detail: Collections the house names for the week: Armand Hammer: The Private Collection; Expanding Horizons: The Hedreen Collection; Shaping Modernity: Property from a Private American Collection; Picasso’s Heroic Years: Masterpieces from a Prestigious European Family; Property from the Estate of Charles Dolan; Lenore and Bernard Greenberg: A Gathering of Works; Looking Forward: The Collection of Beverly Grossman. The page does not say which lots belong to which collection.

whispers.about: Sotheby’s The Now and Contemporary Evening Auction, 16 November
whispers.t: Headline lots: Lichtenstein, Reflections on ‘Painter and Model’ (lot 4) US$20m–30m; Kusama, No. 3 P.B. (lot 110) US$10m–15m; Bacon, Self-Portrait (lot 123) US$10m–15m; Cecily Brown, Untitled (Shipwreck) (lot 6) US$7m–10m; Nara, Candy Blue Night (lot 118) US$5m–7m; de Kooning, Untitled (lot 113) US$4.5m–6.5m.
whispers.detail: Also listed: Mark Bradford, If Caught Outside (lot 120) US$2.5m–3.5m; Warhol, Flowers (lot 101) US$2.5m–3.5m; Frankenthaler, Black Touch (lot 111) US$2.5m–3.5m and Five (lot 138) US$1.5m–2m; Morris Louis, Delta Gamma (lot 137) US$1.2m–1.8m. The sale’s own catalogue page returned no readable text (JavaScript-rendered), so lot-level guarantee symbols could not be read.

whispers.about: Sotheby’s, Vision: The Extraordinary Collection of Theodore and Ruth Baum
whispers.t: Sotheby’s is selling the Theodore and Ruth Baum collection in an evening and a day auction during the week (exhibition 7–15 November; sale dates not stated on the marquee page).
whispers.detail: Highlights the house lists without estimates: Rothko, Untitled (1967); Joan Mitchell, Green Book of Barbara Guest (1960); Ed Ruscha, Dimple (1964); Warhol, The Scream (After Edvard Munch) (1984); Alberto Burri, GA1 (1954); Lucio Fontana, Concetto Spaziale, Attese (1960).

whispers.about: Phillips New York, Modern & Contemporary Art Evening Sale
whispers.t: Phillips’ Evening Sale is estimated in excess of US$70.4m across 23 lots, which the house calls a 50% rise on the previous year’s low estimate; nearly 90% of the works are at auction for the first time.
whispers.detail: Robert Manley, chairman of Modern and Contemporary Art, is quoted. The release gives Tuesday 17 November at 4.30pm ET; the sale’s own page, read on 13 November, gives 18 November at 5pm ET at 432 Park Avenue (see the separate item on the date conflict). Morning Session Thursday 19 November 10am ET (117 works, led by Joan Mitchell, Composition, c. 1965); Afternoon Session 19 November 2pm ET (96 lots, led by Mark Grotjahn, Untitled (Large Colored Butterfly with Smile White Background 9 Wings), 2005). No guarantees are mentioned in the release.

whispers.t: Modigliani’s limestone Tête (carved 1911–12), nearly 30 inches tall and in one private collection for over five decades, is estimated at US$28m–35m, the highest-value sculpture Phillips has offered.
whispers.detail: Other Evening Sale lots in the release: Hockney, David, Celia, Stephen and Ian, London (1982), an eight-panel portrait at auction for the first time; Frank Stella, Port Tampa City (1963), one of thirteen Dartmouth Paintings, from Robert Mnuchin; Clyfford Still, PH-589 (1959); Pollock, Constellation (1946, Accabonac Creek series), ex Peggy Guggenheim and Harold Rosenberg; Frankenthaler, Seabreeze (1980) and Peacock Alley (1990); Miyoko Ito, Odyssey (1959) as lot 1; works by Derek Fordjour, Avery Singer, Rashid Johnson and Joseph Yaeger. A single-owner FREESTYLE sale (a private New York collection) follows on 12 December alongside the Design sale.

whispers.t: Phillips’ two own pages disagree on the Evening Sale: the 2 November release says Tuesday 17 November, 4.30pm ET; the sale page (NY010726), read on 13 November, says 18 November, 5pm ET, at 432 Park Avenue, with viewing 7–18 November.
whispers.detail: The sale page also records a highlights tour: London, 30 Berkeley Square, 8–15 October 2026; Los Angeles, 9041 Nemo Street, 13–15 October 2026. The sale page lists no lots and no guarantee symbols in the text returned. A desk should confirm the time with the house before bidding arrangements.

whispers.t: Sotheby’s announced a 12-painting Impressionist collection expected to fetch in the region of US$450m and said it had guaranteed the collection; Helena Newman declined to disclose the amount.
whispers.detail: Anny Shaw reported that the collection was formed by Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier and Carlos Pedro Blaquier and kept at the family estate, La Biznaga, outside Buenos Aires. Newman, Sotheby’s chairman of Impressionist and Modern art, said the collection was expected ‘in the region of $450m’, adding ‘Plus, maybe plus’. Lots and estimates as reported: Cézanne, Arlequin (1888–90), around US$120m; Van Gogh, Châtaignier en fleurs roses et blanches (May 1890), US$180m; Pissarro, La Place du Théâtre-Français, soleil d’après-midi en hiver (1898), US$30m–40m; Renoir, En Canot (Jeune fille à la barque) (1877), US$25m–35m; Monet, Le Jardin des Tuileries (1876), US$15m–20m; Vlaminck, Nature morte à la cruche bleue (1906–07), US$2m–3m.
whispers.outcome: Sale set for 18 November 2026 at 6pm.

whispers.t: Helena Newman said the Van Gogh could reach US$200m or more and that Sotheby’s expects it to beat the artist’s auction record of US$117m (Orchard with Cypresses, Christie’s New York, 2022, Paul Allen collection).
whispers.detail: Newman described the market as ‘almost like a return to order’ and said ‘what we’re seeing is a return of interest in the very top blue-chip quality’; ‘at public auction, there hasn’t been anything at this level’. The picture was last shown publicly at the Guggenheim, New York, in 1964. It was not shown in London on 30 September because of ‘scheduling issues’, with plans to include it later in the tour.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (Anny Shaw), quoting Helena Newman of Sotheby’s
whispers.outcome: Pending: sale 18 November 2026.

whispers.t: A dispute with Argentine customs officials over the export of about a dozen paintings to Luxembourg in 2023 was resolved earlier in 2026, according to Sotheby’s as reported by The Art Newspaper.
whispers.detail: The lawful course was followed as reported: the matter was settled with the authority before consignment. The family is reported to be retaining its Argentine and Latin American holdings while releasing the Impressionist core; Newman called the sale part of ‘a generational change’. Five works were shown at Sotheby’s London on 30 September 2026, with the tour going on to Taipei, Hong Kong and Paris before New York.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (Anny Shaw), citing Sotheby’s

whispers.t: The Art Newspaper reported that Carlos Pedro Blaquier was charged in 2012 in Argentina over alleged participation in kidnappings during the 1976 military dictatorship; he denied the allegations and died in 2023 without standing trial.
whispers.detail: Stated only as The Art Newspaper states it; no court outcome exists because the case did not reach trial. Nelly Arrieta de Blaquier, reported sole heir to the Ledesma sugar company, chaired the Friends of Argentina’s National Museum of Fine Arts and died in 2020; Carlos Pedro Blaquier was president of Ledesma from 1970 to 2013. The couple were reported to have separated decades ago.

whispers.about: Cézanne and Van Gogh, private-sale comparables
whispers.t: The Art Newspaper noted that Qatar reportedly paid more than US$250m for Cézanne’s The Card Players in a 2012 private sale, and that Van Gogh’s The Zouave (1888), handled by Christie’s, reportedly sold privately for around US$190m.
whispers.detail: Both figures are carried as ‘reportedly’ in the source; neither has a public record. The auction records that matter for the week are Van Gogh US$117.2m (2022) and Cézanne US$137.79m (2022), both from the Paul Allen sale at Christie’s New York.

whispers.about: Sotheby’s 18 November, the two top lots
whispers.t: Carlie Porterfield’s pick of the November auctions carries Van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs (1890) at ‘in the region of $180m’ and Cézanne’s Arlequin (1888–90) at ‘around $120m’, and says the Cézanne could set an artist record if it exceeds its estimate.
whispers.detail: The Van Gogh, painted in the final weeks of the artist’s life at Auvers-sur-Oise, has been in the collection since 1975 and not seen publicly since. The Cézanne is one of four harlequins according to Sotheby’s; earlier owners Vollard, Durand-Ruel and Paul Rosenberg; it hung for two decades at Merton Hall, Cambridge; another version is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. The piece mentions no guarantees, irrevocable bids or withdrawals.
whispers.outcome: Pending: 18 November.

whispers.t: The Art Newspaper’s autumn preview of 12 November 2026 (Carlie Porterfield) is teased on the paper’s site as putting the November week at US$2.4bn; the preview itself could not be opened in this session.
whispers.detail: The figure is carried only as the teaser on two Art Newspaper pages states it (a sidebar on the May 2026 preview and a related-links box on the 2 November piece). For comparison, the paper’s May 2026 preview put the spring week at US$1.8bn–2.6bn across four houses.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (teaser for Carlie Porterfield’s 12 Nov 2026 preview)
src: The Art Newspaper, 11 May 2026 (sidebar teaser dated 12 Nov 2026)

whispers.about: Christie’s Paris, Collection Roger Thérond, 13 November
whispers.t: Christie’s Paris sells the collection of Roger Thérond, longtime editor of Paris Match, on 13 November; Man Ray’s Le Baiser (c. 1930), with Lee Miller as the sitter on the left, is estimated at €250,000–350,000.
whispers.detail: Reported in The Art Newspaper’s pick of the November auctions. It is the one Paris sale in the paper’s pick for the fortnight before New York.

whispers.t: Christie’s will sell Property from the Collection of Wilma (Billie) and Laurence Tisch across its New York Marquee Week of 17–20 November 2026, led by Henry Moore’s Seated Figure at US$5m–8m, with some works going to London and later inclusions slated for 2027.
whispers.detail: Galerie reported the works spread across the 20th Century Evening Sale and the Impressionist and Modern and Post-War and Contemporary day sales; Barry Flanagan’s Six Foot Leaping Hare on Steel Pyramid opens a Modern British Art Evening Sale. Other artists named: Picasso (Femme assise), Léger, Dubuffet (Gens et lieux, 1976), Arp (Grand personnage, 1957), Noguchi. Moore’s record is US$34.9m (King and Queen, Christie’s London, March 2026). The article mislabels a Christie’s executive as Sotheby’s and gives two dates for the Moore, so carry the detail as secondary. Christie’s own page for the week returned only a bot-check script.

whispers.t: Art Basel Qatar’s 2027 list has 82 galleries, down from 87; 35 of the 2026 exhibitors, about 40%, are not returning, among them Hauser & Wirth, Pace, Almine Rech, Victoria Miro and Gallery Isabelle (Dubai).
whispers.detail: Kabir Jhala reported the dates (28–30 January 2027, VIP days 26–27 January, at M7 and Doha Design District), 30 newcomers including Isla Flotante, Pilar Corrias and Silverlens, and the theme ‘between’ under artistic director Wassan Al-Khudhairi, who succeeds Wael Shawky. The full list of non-returners in the article also includes Gladstone, kurimanzutto, Esther Schipper, Karma, Massimodecarlo, David Kordansky, Galerie Chantal Crousel, Galerie Lelong, Waddington Custot and Van de Weghe. Art Basel gave no reason for any gallery’s absence and would not confirm whether geopolitics played a role; Vincenzo De Bellis attributed turnover to the theme-led selection: ‘Across our global fairs, we see greater turnover in the sectors that are theme-led, and in Qatar that approach extends to the fair as a whole.’

whispers.about: Art Basel Qatar, the Gulf risk and the contingency terms
whispers.t: As The Art Newspaper states it: Iran launched missiles into Qatar in late February 2026, weeks after the first fair, injuring 16 people according to Qatari authorities; Saudi Arabia was bombarded in October 2026; exhibitors get a refund or deferral to January 2028 if the fair is postponed, and a standard penalty applies to last-minute withdrawals.
whispers.detail: Support package: Qatar Sports Investments and QC+ (Qatar Museums’ commercial arm) fund customs clearance, local transport, storage, installation, hotel stays for up to two staff and artist travel; from 2027 the fair covers 50% of outbound shipping of unsold works, up to US$20,000 per gallery. Noah Horowitz spoke of a year-round programme of masterclasses and workshops; the Rubaiya quadrennial opens alongside the fair with more than 120 artists, including Saodat Ismailova and Rirkrit Tiravanija.

whispers.about: London benchmark: Sotheby’s Contemporary Evening Sale, 15 October 2026
whispers.t: Sotheby’s London Contemporary Evening Sale made £36.9m hammer against a £39.5m low estimate (£45.9m with fees), 82% sold, six of 34 lots unsold, three withdrawn; de Kooning’s Untitled (1977), guaranteed, hammered at £8.2m (£9.8m with fees), a European auction record for the artist.
whispers.detail: Auctioneer Tom Eddison. Richter, Abstraktes Bild (1992), £5.4m hammer (£6.7m) below its £6m low; Rothko, Untitled (1969), guaranteed, £3m hammer (£3.8m) to an online bidder; Hockney, Henry Reading (1985), guaranteed, £2.3m (£2.8m); a 2021 Hockney iPad drawing £1.5m hammer (£1.9m), an iPad record; Baselitz, P.D. Idol (1964), guaranteed, £1.9m (£2.4m); Michael Andrews, Butterfly Fish (1978), £550,000 (£704,000), a works-on-paper record. About 30% of lots hammered above low estimate. Last October’s equivalent sale made £47.6m. Sotheby’s London 2026 to date: US$1bn across categories; modern and contemporary £598m (US$793m), the highest year-to-date since 2015.

whispers.about: London benchmark: Kusama and the ultra-contemporary
whispers.t: At Sotheby’s London a 2021 Kusama wall sculpture hammered at £250,000, a quarter of its £1m low estimate (£320,000 with fees); Lynette Yiadom-Boakye (£600,000–900,000) and Jadé Fadojutimi (£350,000–450,000) went unsold.
whispers.detail: Thomas Stauffer (Gerber & Stauffer Fine Arts, Zurich; president of the Swiss Art Market Association) said collectors are ‘not willing to take big risks’, called the Fadojutimi and Yiadom-Boakye results ‘concerning’ for the ultra-contemporary segment, called the Kusama result a ‘little scratch’, questioned the presale valuation and called the consignor’s consent to sell far below estimate ‘mysterious’. Read against Sotheby’s New York Kusama, No. 3 P.B., at US$10m–15m on 16 November.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (Vivienne Chow), quoting Thomas Stauffer

whispers.t: Christie’s London opened the October week with £178m hammer (£218.6m with fees; Keith Gill cited £219m) across the Monsoon single-owner sale and the 20th/21st Century Evening Sale; the Peter Simon collection made £86.9m (£107.5m with fees), the highest-value single-owner collection sold at Christie’s London, with all 41 lots guaranteed (11 by the house, the rest by third parties) and 98% sold.
whispers.detail: Monsoon top lots: Bacon, Figure in Movement (1978), £14.5m (£17.2m), bought from Ivor Braka in 2006, sold to a woman in the room; Mondrian, Composition A, with Double Line and Yellow (1935), £8m (£9.7m); Miró, Peinture (Les amants – Adam et Eve) (1925), £7m (£8.6m), auction debut; Popova, Painterly Architectonic (1918), record £6.2m (£7.6m) against a £1.8m low; Hurvin Anderson, Last House (2013), £4.6m (£5.7m). Records for Portia Zvavahera (£307,200), Bridget Riley (£5.2m), David Bomberg (£3.3m) and a painting record for Barbara Hepworth (£537,600). The only unsold lot was a 1967 Auerbach. Rebecca Wei called it ‘a steady, solid sale, with active bidding throughout’.

whispers.about: London benchmark: Christie’s 20th/21st Century Evening Sale, 14 October 2026
whispers.t: The evening sale made £90.5m hammer (£111.1m with fees) against adjusted estimates of £86m–126m, 46 lots after five withdrawals, seven bought in (85% sold); Kandinsky’s Das bunte Leben (1907), restituted in June 2023 to the heirs of Hedwig Lewenstein-Weyermann and third-party guaranteed, hammered at £27m (£31.6m) above its £25m high estimate; Mondrian’s Composition III (1920), fresh to market and third-party guaranteed, hammered at £21.5m (£25.2m).
whispers.detail: The Kandinsky went to a phone bidder represented by Maria Los after six minutes; the Mondrian to a phone bidder represented by Katharine Arnold. Igshaan Adams set a record at £96,000 with proceeds to Artists for Climate Action. The equivalent sale made £106.9m in October 2025 and £114.2m in March 2026, so the October 2026 evening sale was lower than both despite the paper’s framing. Keith Gill said the results ‘further reinforce London’s position as a key international market for museum-quality masterpieces’.

whispers.about: The year’s benchmark: ArtTactic on the first half of 2026
whispers.t: ArtTactic put first-half 2026 sales at the three houses at US$6.8bn, up 70% year on year (Christie’s US$3.4bn, Sotheby’s US$2.8bn, Phillips US$505.4m), the best first half since 2022; London up 131% to US$1.42bn, Hong Kong up almost 30% to US$764m, sell-through 91% with 131 white-glove sales.
whispers.detail: Relayed by October Gallery from The Art Newspaper’s report of 10 July 2026; car sales excluded. The June Lewis collection sale at Sotheby’s London brought US$390m, about 28% of London’s half. Anders Petterson: the recovery is ‘proving to be far broader than the headline-grabbing results at the very top end’; ‘luxury consumption tends to follow asset prices rather than GDP or consumer confidence’. Heritage Auctions separately reported a record H1 of US$1.4bn.
whispers.who: October Gallery, relaying The Art Newspaper (10 Jul 2026) on ArtTactic

whispers.about: Hong Kong autumn: Christie’s 20th/21st Century Evening Sale, 29 September 2026
whispers.t: Christie’s Hong Kong autumn evening sale (29 September, The Henderson) was led by Basquiat’s Ancient Scientist (1984) at HK$56m–76m (US$7.1m–9.7m), Kusama’s A-Pumpkin (YHP) (2011) at HK$48m–68m (US$6.1m–8.7m) and Zao Wou-Ki’s Voie lactée – 09.11.56 at HK$45m–75m (US$5.7m–9.6m).
whispers.detail: Also: Richter, Abstraktes Bild (1991), HK$38m–55m; Chu Teh-Chun, Automne (1985), HK$25m–35m, auction debut; Cézanne, L’Assiette bleue (1878–80), HK$25m–35m, Hong Kong debut; Matisse, Jeune femme au canapé (1944), HK$20m–30m; Liu Ye, Blue Sea (1998), HK$16m–26m; day sales 30 September led by Nara, Q&A (1995), HK$12m–18m. The page is labelled an advertisement feature sponsored by Christie’s, so it is the house’s own pre-sale framing. Results were not opened in this session (see unconfirmed).
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (advertisement feature, sponsored by Christie’s)
whispers.outcome: Sale held 29 September 2026; totals not confirmed here.

whispers.t: Yayoi Kusama died in August 2026 at the age of 97, as The Art Newspaper’s Hong Kong feature states; her works were offered in Hong Kong in September and London in October, and Sotheby’s New York offers No. 3 P.B. at US$10m–15m on 16 November.
whispers.detail: The London reading (a 2021 wall sculpture hammered at a quarter of its low estimate on 15 October) and the Hong Kong headline seen but not opened (‘Kusama works get a cool reception’, South China Morning Post) suggest the estate-driven supply question will be tested in New York. Carried only as the sponsored feature states the death; the obituary itself was not opened.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (sponsored feature); The Art Newspaper (Vivienne Chow) for London

whispers.about: Hong Kong benchmark: spring 2026 evening sales
whispers.t: ArtTactic’s spring 2026 Hong Kong report puts the three houses’ marquee evening sales at HK$991.5m (US$126.6m), a rebound after four years of decline, with all three houses meeting or exceeding presale estimates.
whispers.detail: ArtTactic, Auction Analysis: Hong Kong Marquee Evening Auctions – March 2026 (43 pages, analysts Lindsay Dewar Leite and James Cocksey), £195 single report or £1,195 a year on the Analyst Pro membership. The ArtTactic/Mishcon de Reya China Market Report 2026 separately records Hong Kong’s highest sales volume in a decade in 2025 (22,247 lots), a 14.5% share of global auction sales (third after New York and London), modern and contemporary value down 30% and traditional Asian works up 32.4%.
whispers.who: ArtTactic (report page); Ocula on the ArtTactic/Mishcon de Reya report
src: ArtTactic, Hong Kong Marquee Evening Auctions March 2026
Ocula, Hong Kong auction volumes reach ten-year high

whispers.t: Art Basel Miami Beach runs 4–6 December 2026 (VIP previews 2–3 December) with 272 exhibitors; the Galleries sector is cut about 10% to 204 from 226 in 2025, the footprint is about 12% smaller, and the plazas go from five to four, with blue-chip galleries spread across the floor.
whispers.detail: Carlie Porterfield named galleries absent in 2026: Commonwealth and Council, Night Gallery, Gallery Hyundai, Gallery Wendi Norris, kurimanzutto, Pippy Houldsworth, Richard Saltoun, Ellie Rines (formerly 56 Henry). Returning: Gagosian, White Cube, Pace, Hauser & Wirth; South Florida’s Fredric Snitzer, David Castillo, Gavlak, Nina Johnson. More than 30 first-time exhibitors; more than two-thirds of galleries have spaces in the Americas. Zero 10 returns with Generation (19 projects; Jon Rafman, Refik Anadol, Sarah Meyohas), curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman; Nicole Sales Giles is the first global head of Zero 10. Bridget Finn: ‘the smaller footprint is a deliberate choice in service of that’. Art Basel’s own announcement page returned a server error.

whispers.t: Tim Schneider counted at least 26 dealers that downgraded their real estate or closed between 1 January and 21 July 2026; Gagosian is giving up 28–29 Burlington Arcade and its only Basel gallery (July 2026), David Zwirner is leaving 69th Street (Artnet News, July 2026), Pace is seeking a smaller London space than 5 Hanover Square (FT, June 2026), and Hauser & Wirth opens Palo Alto on 3 October while keeping 17 spaces.
whispers.detail: Hauser & Wirth’s co-founders sold the 69th Street townhouse for a reported US$10.5m (Artnet News, May 2025). Adam Green (Dallas adviser): ‘The softening on the primary market has impacted every gallery, regardless of size’; ‘the top galleries have more levers to pull, whether that’s closing a location or cutting staff.’ Alain Servais: ‘The art market infrastructure is sized for selling a lot of rubbish at high prices’ and ‘more dramatic rightsizing will be necessary, particularly to compete with more efficient auction houses’.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper, The Insiders blog (Tim Schneider), citing Artnet News, the FT and gallery spokespeople

whispers.t: Hyperallergic, citing ARTnews’ reading of UK filings, reported that Pace lost US$5.4m last year and is carrying out a US$19.2m debt-for-equity swap with its US parent; citing the New York Times, that Pace laid off 50 staff and dropped 50 artists over the summer; Pace closed Hong Kong in October 2025 and listed its 8,600 sq ft London space for rent in June.
whispers.detail: Lakshmi Rivera Amin’s Art Movements column, 5 November 2026. Multiple Pace employees told Hyperallergic they learned of the cuts from the Times in early June; an unnamed artist called it ‘a callous breach of trust’. The column carries no comment from Pace and does not name the Glimchers. Pace is also among the galleries not returning to Art Basel Qatar in 2027 (The Art Newspaper, 27 Oct 2026) but is returning to Miami Beach (The Art Newspaper, 29 Sep 2026).
whispers.who: Hyperallergic (Lakshmi Rivera Amin), citing ARTnews and the New York Times

whispers.t: Gordon VeneKlasen, formerly of Michael Werner Gallery, opened his own gallery in New York and London with two Sigmar Polke shows (New York: Sigmar Polke: The Dream of Menelaus), as The Baer Faxt’s No Reserve letter reported in April 2026.
whispers.detail: Kenny Schachter’s column of 25 November 2025 (originally on Artnet News, republished on his site) had reported ‘the dissolution of the partnership’ at Michael Werner, VeneKlasen’s planned move and the closing of the gallery’s Los Angeles outpost; it also carried claims from unnamed current and former employees that VeneKlasen and the gallery did not answer. Those claims are not repeated here. Older than the fortnight; carried as background to the gallery map.
whispers.who: No Reserve from The Baer Faxt (issue 33); Kenny Schachter (Artnet News column, 25 Nov 2025)
src: No Reserve from The Baer Faxt, issue 33, 28 Apr 2026

whispers.about: Last year’s benchmark: New York, November 2025
whispers.t: November 2025 in New York: Christie’s took US$690m on its first night (anchored by the Robert F. and Patricia G. Ross Weis collection) and US$123.6m in its 21st Century sale; Sotheby’s Modern Evening made US$527.5m with the Leonard A. Lauder collection, led by Klimt’s Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer at US$236.4m, the second-highest auction price ever, and Kahlo’s El sueño (La cama) at US$54.7m; Sotheby’s Now and Contemporary made US$178.5m against US$143.6m–198.25m; Phillips made US$67.3m with 94% sold.
whispers.detail: Elephant, relaying The Art Daddy’s reporting: ‘This week belonged to supply, not sentiment.’ Christie’s 20th Century: Rothko US$62.2m, Matisse US$32.3m, Chagall US$26.5m, Ernst US$20.2m; more than twenty lots sold below estimate, three failed. At Sotheby’s the Kerry James Marshall and Barkley Hendricks lots failed and Cattelan’s gold toilet sold at the opening bid; Cecily Brown set a record at US$9.8m. Artprice’s annual report confirms the Klimt at US$236,360,000 as 2025’s record. Phillips’ 2026 Evening Sale estimate (in excess of US$70.4m) is to be read against this US$67.3m result.
whispers.who: Elephant (relaying The Art Daddy); Artmarket.com/Artprice release

whispers.about: This year’s spring benchmark: New York, May 2026 (as previewed)
whispers.t: The Art Newspaper’s May 2026 preview put the spring week at US$1.8bn–2.6bn: Sotheby’s US$690.4m–942.5m (Robert Mnuchin sale, est. whispers.about: The year’s frame: Art Basel and UBS Global Art Market Report 2026
whispers.t: Global art sales rose 4% to US$59.6bn in 2025 (41.5m transactions, up 2%): dealers US$34.8bn (up 2%), public auctions US$20.7bn (up 9%), private sales just under US$4.2bn (down 5%); US 44% (US$26.0bn), UK 18% (US$10.5bn), China 14% (US$8.5bn), France 8% (US$4.5bn); fine-art lots over US$1m up 21% in value and sales above US$10m up 30%; online sales US$9.2bn, the lowest since 2019.
whispers.detail: Dr Clare McAndrew (Arts Economics) for Art Basel and UBS; relayed the same day by Artlyst. Auction sectors: Post-war US$3.1bn (down 3%, 31% share); Modern US$2.4bn (up 9%); Contemporary US$1.4bn (flat); Impressionist and Post-Impressionist up 47% (19% share); Old Masters just under US$1.2bn (up 30%). Artprice’s own count of fine-art auctions puts 2025 at US$11.1bn, up 12%, with the US at 42% and an unsold rate of 32%.
src: Art Basel, Global Art Market Report 2026

whispers.about: Track record: HENI’s call on November 2025
whispers.t: HENI News wrote on 5 November 2025 that ‘even a modest rebound would lift the HENI Auction Index this November’ after grades of D (May 2024), C- (November 2024) and C- (May 2025); the week then produced the Klimt at US$236.4m and Christie’s US$690m first night.
whispers.detail: HENI’s metrics at the time: about 2.7 bidders per lot against a 2.8 twenty-week average; about 60% of lots hammering above low estimate; marquee weeks of 16 sales and about 1,700 lots; recent weeks at US$1.3bn–1.5bn against a US$2bn historical average. The May 2025 Riggio sale at Christie’s was 100% guaranteed with 47% of lots ‘weak’ (at or below low estimate). HENI’s own November 2025 follow-up (‘New York’s Marquee Week Gets Its Mojo Back’) appeared in search results but was not opened.
whispers.outcome: Borne out: see the November 2025 benchmark item.

whispers.about: Track record: Kenny Schachter’s November 2025 buyer claims
whispers.t: Kenny Schachter wrote (Artnet News, 25 November 2025) that, per his sources, Ken Griffin was an underbidder on the Klimt and two Asian buyers took the two Klimt landscapes; stated as fact that François Pinault bought Lauder’s Agnes Martin for US$17.6m via Philippe Ségalot and that Pierre Chen bought Christie’s Hockney double portrait on a US$38m guarantee; said he ‘suspect[s]’ Eduardo Costantini bought the Kahlo but was ‘not yet certain’.
whispers.detail: Carried as the column labels each claim: sourced, stated, or suspected. None was confirmed by the houses in the column; a Black representative did not respond and the parties denied the Klimt rumour. The column also claimed Steve Cohen consigned the gold toilet and Wool’s Untitled (RIOT); Point72 did not reply. Useful as a worked example of how the trade’s rumour sheet reads, and of what to check before repeating it.
whispers.who: Kenny Schachter (Artnet News column, republished on kennyschachter.art)
whispers.outcome: Unverified in this session.

whispers.about: Hong Kong autumn result: Christie’s 20th/21st Century Evening Sale, 29 September 2026
whispers.t: Christie’s Hong Kong evening sale made HK$726.4m with premium, up 28% on the year, with all 50 lots sold after two withdrawals (100% by lot); Basquiat’s Ancient Scientist hammered at HK$62.5m (HK$76.975m with premium), Zao Wou-Ki’s Voie lactée at HK$47.5m (HK$58.85m) and Kusama’s A-Pumpkin (YHP) at HK$47m, just under its HK$48m low estimate (HK$58.24m with premium); no lot passed HK$100m.
whispers.detail: Reported by Bijutsu Techō (Tokyo) the day after the sale. Kusama’s Infinity-Nets [WUPT] (2016) made HK$18.56m against HK$13m–20m. The Basquiat last sold at Phillips Hong Kong in 2020 for HK$58.33m; Christie’s called it the top price of the Asian autumn so far. The previous two autumn sales each had a lot above HK$100m (Picasso’s Buste de femme HK$196.75m in 2025; Monet HK$233.38m and Van Gogh HK$250.63m in 2024). Arkou Yu, Christie’s Asia Pacific head of the evening sale, told the magazine before the sale that no major change was yet visible after Kusama’s death, that heirs and collectors were unlikely to sell in a rush and that prices were ‘fairly stable’. The same report relays Sotheby’s Hong Kong’s two sales (28 September) at about ¥14.8bn, with 15 Foujita works at about ¥1.35bn. The South China Morning Post’s season wrap (‘Hong Kong autumn 2026 art auctions top HK$2 billion as Kusama works get a cool reception’) refused to open.

whispers.about: The law this fortnight: a Paris court cancels a 2024 Sotheby’s London sale
whispers.t: On 5 November 2026 a Paris court ordered the restitution to the seven heirs of Salomon Flavian of Pissarro’s Darse de pêche et bassin Duquesne (1902), looted in Paris in 1941 and sold at Sotheby’s London on 25 June 2024 for £1.2m; it cancelled the sale and gave Sotheby’s two months to disclose the buyer’s complete identity, on a €1,000 daily penalty.
whispers.detail: Vincent Noce reported that the painting was in Flavian’s collection from 1935 and registered in the French government’s looted-art repertory in 1947; the court found ‘no direct and convincing evidence’ of the Paul Rosenberg to Edward Le Bas transfer argued by Sotheby’s and the Toronto restitution firm Mondex Corporation, and dismissed the claims against Sotheby’s while leaving a 2024 agreement between Mondex and two heirs in place. Corinne Hershkovitch (heirs’ lawyer): ‘It is a very important ruling, which opens the way to a restitution that the Flavian family has demanded since the war.’ Sotheby’s London said it was ‘disappointed by the judgement regarding the restitution’ but ‘welcomes the decision to dismiss all claims against Sotheby’s’. Mondex’s lawyer Melina Wolman said it would appeal. The lawful course for a desk: check the French repertory and the Lost Art and Commission for Looted Art registries before consignment; enforcement in the UK requires a further procedure, and the possessor could seek compensation from Sotheby’s if the heirs succeed.
whispers.outcome: Ruling 5 Nov 2026; appeal announced by Mondex; Sotheby’s considering joining.

whispers.about: Lawsuits pending: Alison Jacques gallery, London
whispers.t: Yoed and Natasha Anise are suing Alison Jacques gallery in the Central London County Court over a cancelled October 2023 purchase of three Monica Sjöö paintings bought for £264,000; the gallery has counterclaimed; the hearing is due in March 2027.
whispers.detail: Vittoria Benzine reported the claim as filed: a refund of £264,000 plus the £66,000 discount, the adviser’s US$31,944 fee, £9,091 travel costs and a provisional £26,400 for loss of ‘pleasure, amenity, prestige and heritage value’; the buyers say they were misled about the circumstances. The gallery denies breach of contract, concedes in its counterclaim that title passed on payment and that an earlier statement to the contrary was ‘incorrect’, and alleges it was misled about the buyers’ ‘credentials’. The paintings remain in storage at the gallery after Modern Art Oxford returned them in February 2024.
whispers.outcome: Pending; hearing March 2027.

whispers.t: Cahn v. Sotheby’s, No. 659868/2025, filed 19 November 2025 in the Supreme Court of New York: collector Charles C. Cahn Jr. seeks US$2.67m plus interest for alleged breach of a November 2016 agreement over a painting attributed to Modigliani, Portrait de Leopold Zborowski (1917), which Sotheby’s sold him in 2003 for about US$1.55m.
whispers.detail: The Center for Art Law’s case review (Vivianne Diaz) states the complaint’s allegations, including that Sotheby’s told Cahn in 2016 that the work’s authenticity was in doubt, and notes that Cahn had offered no evidence for these claims; Sotheby’s had not yet answered at the time of the review. No outcome is reported. Carried as the court record and the review state it.
whispers.outcome: Pending as of January 2026.

whispers.detail: Background from The Art Newspaper’s earlier reporting (seen in search, not opened): Cerutti stepped down as chief executive in January 2025 with Bonnie Brennan succeeding, and Alex Rotter became global president in May 2025. whispers.t: Bonhams was sold by Epiris to Pemberton Asset Management for an undisclosed sum, with Seth Johnson joining as chief executive, Liese Thomas as chief financial officer and Jennifer Babington as chief operating officer; Chabi Nouri left as chief executive after a year and Céline Assimon stepped down as chief commercial officer.
whispers.detail: Kabir Jhala’s report. Epiris had bought Bonhams in 2018 and sought a US$1bn valuation in 2023. Chairman Hans-Kristian Hoejsgaard said the appointees had a ‘proven track record of success in serving high value customers’. Bonhams’ November 2026 New York sales could not be found in this session; its November 2025 evening sale made US$17m (90% sold) with the Gene Hackman collection at US$1.64m (Bonhams press release, undated page).
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (Kabir Jhala); Bonhams press release

whispers.about: The year’s reading: guarantees and the K-shaped market
whispers.t: Scott Reyburn reported that 61% of evening-sale lots in the autumn 2025 New York auctions were guaranteed, that works over US$1m have made 77% of sales value at the three houses over ten years while being 7% of lots (Anders Petterson, ArtTactic), and that the US$2.2bn November total was still 30% below 2022’s US$3.2bn.
whispers.detail: Petterson: ‘we’re likely to see the flow again’ in the US$1m-plus segment in 2026; Wendy Cromwell expected the contraction in galleries to ease over time. Cecily Brown (Christie’s, US$4m–6m) and Jadé Fadojutimi (Phillips, US$800,000–1.2m) lots failed in November 2025; Artprice data showed one of four Fadojutimi works over US$300,000 sold since May 2025. The piece notes two new fairs for 2026: Art Basel Qatar (February) and Frieze Abu Dhabi (November). The US$2.2bn figure is attributed to Sotheby’s Madeline Lissner in Puck.
whispers.who: The Art Newspaper (Scott Reyburn), citing ArtTactic, Artprice and Puck

whispers.about: Track record closed: HENI graded November 2025 an A
whispers.t: HENI’s Auction Index gave New York’s November 2025 marquee week an A, its strongest since spring 2022, on more than US$2.2bn across 18 sales and 1,700-plus lots: Sotheby’s A+ (about US$1.2bn), Christie’s B, Phillips B-; strong guarantees ran at three times the level of comparable weeks and weak ones at about twice.
whispers.detail: Lots hammering above estimate ran about 10% above typical; bought-ins and withdrawals fell below average. Withers’ Fiduciary Eye (November 2025) counted 16 works above US$20m and six above US$50m, against six and none in May 2025, and observed that many top lots sold on single bids to third-party guarantors, questioning whether some estimates were set too high. These are the figures this week’s results will be read against.
whispers.who: HENI News; Withers (The Fiduciary Eye: Mari-Claudia Jiménez and Frank K. Lord IV)
